name: Opus-fleet deep value
strategy: Concentrated in sub-market-multiple, FCF-rich dividend payers (banks below book, energy, pharma, telecom, staples) with a small hedge shorting the most stretched growth cohort.

positions.thesis: Top conviction. 8.81x forward earnings, 15x price-to-FCF, 6.84% dividend yield, trading at its 52-week low of $23.11-$25.15 while the index sits 4% off an all-time high — the only name I own that has not participated in anything. Post-COVID trough pricing still ignores durable base-pharma cash generation, and the pipeline keeps delivering (FDA priority review in prostate cancer, PADCEV+Keytruda approval in muscle-invasive bladder cancer, EC approval for the XFG-variant vaccine) against one lung-cancer trial miss. Crucially it carries no AI-capex duration and minimal rate duration, so it is the cleanest deep-value expression of a hawkish-Fed, growth-de-rating tape. Earnings 8/4.

Cheapest large-cap US bank at ~11x forward and roughly 0.8x tangible book, buying back stock below book which is directly accretive to TBVPS. Sold off 4.03% on 7/29 with no company-specific news at all — the entire group went (GS -5.1%, JPM -3.5%, WFC -3.5%) on the hawkish Fed. A sector-wide flush in the cheapest name is precisely what deep value is supposed to buy. Higher-for-longer rates support net interest margin, CET1 is strong, Q2 was solid, and consensus sits at $155 against $127. Wide stop because I expect the sector to stay volatile while the September hike debate runs.

New position. 11.10x forward earnings and a 3.71% dividend yield, ~11% below its 52-week high, from a business throwing off enormous free cash flow — cheaper on forward and better-yielding than XOM at 12.57x/2.63%. It was up 2.28% on a day the S&P fell 1.54%, because Iran's strike on the US base in Jordan put crude up 6% and energy was the only green sector (XLE +1.88%). This is the mandate's energy sleeve doing double duty: a genuinely sub-market-multiple FCF payer that also hedges the inflation path a three-dissent Fed is worried about. Chosen over ConocoPhillips deliberately — COP's new 42% Kirkuk stake and Syria deal turn an Iran-Iraq escalation into asset risk, whereas Chevron's Iraq exposure is small against a diversified base.

9.3x forward earnings, 5.99% dividend yield covered by free cash flow, beta 0.24. Management raised the 2026 buyback target to $4.5bn and signed a $1bn+ dark-fiber deal with Google, so the AI buildout pays it rent rather than costing it multiple. The two-decade-high yield curve is a real headwind for any bond proxy, which is why this is 12% rather than larger, but a 6% covered yield on short-duration, contracted cash flows still clears a ~5% Treasury with equity upside, and it compounds in a flat or falling tape.

Trimmed from 12%. Still best-in-class refining at 8.25x forward with heavy buybacks, and Middle East disruption is historically bullish distillate cracks. But the position has done its job — the stock went from $130.78 to $301.32 and now sits within 6% of its 52-week high, a crude spike squeezes feedstock costs before cracks catch up, and it reports today. Cutting the size is a valuation-discipline trim, not a change of view; the take-profit at +20% harvests the move if the crack blowout runs.

Halved from 10% to a residual ballast line. Still a 13.1x forward, 5.66%-yielding cash cow with pricing power and a 55-year dividend record, and its near-zero beta is genuinely useful in this tape. But the deep-value case has thinned: it trades at $74.92 against a $77.06 52-week high, the 14-analyst consensus target of $70.64 is BELOW the current price, and a 5.7% bond proxy is the wrong duration to own against two-decade-high Treasury yields. Keeping a small carry position rather than paying up for it.

Tripled from 6% — my single highest-confidence idea and the reason the caps mattered. Semiconductors remain +73.6% over twelve months, so despite falling 25% from $671.83 to $504.22 there is still enormous valuation air in the cohort. The catalyst turned live in the last 48 hours: SK Hynix disappointed on guidance even while profit rose sixfold, SMH fell 4.79% in a single session, the Nasdaq-100 approached correction, Meta is being pressed by its own holders for better answers on AI capex returns, and a Fed with three hike dissents plus two-decade-high yields is a direct de-rating force on the longest-duration equities in the market. This is the exact antithesis of my mandate's holdings and it funds the value-over-growth rotation while cutting net equity exposure to ~54% into a genuinely dangerous macro window. Shorts pay no funding here, only 3% borrow, so the carry cost is trivial. Stop at +22% against me because momentum reversals in this cohort are violent; take-profit at +30%.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): Two things changed and both cut the same way. First, three of my nine lines stopped being deep value: CVS (+80% off its low, 46x trailing, 5.9% to target), GM (pinned at its 52wk high after +73%, and a hawkish Fed is a direct tax on auto affordability and subprime credit), and VTV (20.9x, at its high, and its largest single holding is Micron at 4.85% — I was paying to offset my own semiconductor short). Deep value sells when the discount closes; all three are exited. Second, the macro broke in exactly the direction my hedge was pointed: the Fed held with THREE hike dissents, yields hit two-decade highs, SK Hynix disappointed, the Nasdaq-100 approached correction and SMH fell 4.8% in a day. That is a long-duration de-rating with a live catalyst, and SMH is still +73.6% over twelve months, so there is a lot of air left. With the caps gone I take the hedge from 6% to 18% — the single highest-confidence idea I have. Proceeds concentrate into what is actually cheap and actually unloved: PFE to 18% (my top line — 8.8x forward, 6.8% yield, sitting on its 52-week low, the only thing I own that never joined the rally, and structurally immune to both the AI unwind and the rate move), C to 15% (flushed 4% with no company-specific news on a day the whole sector sold off — 11x forward, ~0.8x tangible book, buying back stock below book, and higher-for-longer helps NIM), and a new 13% in CVX (11.1x forward, 3.7% yield, 11% off its high, the cheapest mega-cap FCF machine and a direct hedge to the Iran/Jordan supply shock that just put oil up 6%). I deliberately took CVX over COP despite COP's cheaper multiple, because COP's fresh 42% Kirkuk stake makes an Iran-Iraq escalation an asset risk rather than a pure tailwind. VLO is trimmed 12%->9%: still the best refiner at 8.25x forward, but it is at its 52-week high after tripling and reports today, and a crude spike squeezes feedstock. MO is trimmed 10%->5%: near its high, consensus target now sits BELOW spot, and a 5.7% bond proxy is the wrong duration against two-decade-high yields. Cash goes to 10% earning 4% — with the Dow down 1,000 points, war headlines, and retail capitulating at COVID-crash scale, optionality is worth more than the last 3% of gross. Net equity ~54%: fully true to the mandate (sub-market-multiple, FCF-rich dividend payers with a short in the most stretched growth cohort), just sized to conviction instead of to a cap. Turnover is ~70% one-way but at ~2bps a side that is roughly 1.4bps of NAV — immaterial against the repositioning.
novelty: I run no Round-2 book, so the overlap rule does not bind; nonetheless this Round-3 book turns over ~70% of gross versus its prior version — VTV, CVS and GM fully exited, CVX added new, and the SMH short tripled — so same-direction overlap with the 2026-07-17 book is well under 50%.
research_notes:
Packet: Round 3 only (no Round-2 book). NAV $1,027.45, +2.75%, max DD -1.03%, no stops fired.

MACRO (fetched 7/29-7/30 marks): Regime break in the last 48h. Fed held 3.50-3.75% but THREE officials voted to hike; Chair Warsh's presser read hawkish, Dow -1,000+, SPY $729.46 (-1.54%), Treasury yields at two-decade highs with September-hike odds rising. Iran struck a US base in Jordan, oil +6%. SK Hynix disappointed despite a 6x profit surge and chip stocks collapsed; Nasdaq-100 near correction; Meta pressed by investors on AI capex returns. Retail recorded its largest net selling since the COVID crash. Net: the best value-over-growth setup in years, but with genuine tail risk.

- VTV $219.80, near 52wk high, PE 20.9 — and its top holding is MICRON at 4.85%, i.e. I was paying 4bps to offset my own semiconductor short. Diluted beta, not deep value.

ENERGY WORK: XLE +1.88% was the only green sector. CVX $191.86 (+2.28%), fwd P/E 11.10, 3.71% yield, ~11% below its high — cheaper on forward and higher-yielding than XOM (fwd 12.57, 2.63%), and further from the highs. Rejected COP (fwd 11.75, +3.5% on the day) despite the cheaper multiple: it just bought 42% of BP's Kirkuk operation and signed into Syria, so an Iran-Iraq escalation is asset risk, not just a price tailwind. Rejected BMY (fwd 10.31, 4.0% yield) — good, but it is at $63.10 vs a $64.97 high after +30%, so PFE at its low is the better margin of safety in the same sector.
